rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, nulls and four native designs before any content was read; synthetic validation on the real ledger schedules (4 truths x 30 datasets) with a pre-data Amendment 1; a post-hoc noise-calibrated power check; 27 replication + 4 native folders with verdicts; both embedding models; DQ5 robustness; confirm.py frozen and dry-run (not run). Missing: holdout run, a settling estimator with power, the message-level alpha test.
rationale.faithfulness: The literal claim (settling = time for everyone to read everyone once) fails on magnitude: tau is ~10x the coverage time and ~80x the read-out chain's mixing time. The scaling claim is untested in practice: primaries lose to the constant in both models, but settling is detectable in only 11/27 periods and the real-like synthetic has ~0 power. Natives lean against read-out as the driver (#38, #51) with one weak positive (NE42, gte only). Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D0 E0 F1 G1 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A diagnostic with a negative design implication: in broadcast rooms read-out coverage completes in minutes, so convergence on a new goal is not limited by who has read whom, and room merges or faster calls will not speed it via reading. Ledger coverage times are computable but weakest-link (one silent agent). No lever.

one_line: Agents read each other within minutes but content settles over hours (τ ≈ 10× coverage time); the scaling test has no power at real noise.

v2.claim: In broadcast rooms read-out coverage is far faster than post-kickoff content settling: 90% of room-mate pairs read each other within 0.24 active h, while settling takes about 4.5 h (bge) / 1.9 h (gte) where detectable; tau/T90 is 10.1 (bge) and 4.5 (gte), outside the predicted [1/3, 3], so 'everyone has read everyone once' is not the settling clock. Scaling of settling with bulk read-out time is untested (no power at real noise).

v2.adjudication_note: Different claim scored: the coordinator scored a composite whose second half ('the scaling test is unpowered') drew a not-identifiable penalty (x0.5) and gave decision 'none'; the blind rater scored the magnitude result (P2) with a multiplicity penalty from the 19-predictor scan. Ruling: score only the pre-registered magnitude claim, which is identified and was tested once (no scan multiplicity), and keep the unpowered scaling question out of the claim; V stays low because the claim does not establish that faster reading would not help.
